title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the preceding page, 'Lemme 1 A'): V is a bounded Jordan domain with rectifiable boundary C, and I is a rectifiable topological arc from an interior point a to a boundary point b, with I∩C={b}. The slit domain is U = V \ (I\{b}). Mark 1, ζ = e^{2iπ/3} and ζ̄ on S¹ = ∂D. They cut the circle into three arcs: α from ζ to ζ̄ through −1, β = (1,ζ) and β̄ = (1,ζ̄). The lemma asserts a continuous map f: D̄ → Ū with the following properties: it is a conformal homeomorphism D → U; f(ζ) = f(ζ̄) = b; f maps α minus its endpoints homeomorphically onto C\{b}; f maps each of β and β̄ bijectively onto I, with f(1) = a. Geometrically this is the Carathéodory extension of the Riemann map of a slit domain: the two 'banks' of the slit correspond to the arcs β and β̄.

This page:
- NB1: f is unique, because Aut(D) = PSU(1,1) acts simply transitively on positively ordered triples of distinct points of S¹.
- NB2: condition 3) yields a canonical homeomorphism φ = (f|β̄)^{-1}∘(f|β): β → β̄ with φ(1)=1 and φ(ζ)=ζ̄. φ identifies the two prime-end preimages of each point of the slit, i.e. it is the conformal welding homeomorphism of the slit.
- B): φ is 'rectifiable'. Conversely, every 'rectifiable' homeomorphism φ: β ≅ β̄ should arise this way. Grothendieck normalises by first uniformising V̄ to D̄ (using 'théorème d'uniformisation A' and 'critère I'), then sending a to 0 and b to 1. The claim is then that there exists a continuous f = f_φ: D̄ → D̄, holomorphic and injective on the open disc, realising φ.
- The next page continues with uniqueness and a 'Scholie'. It asserts a bijection between (a) homeomorphisms [0,1]→[0,1] fixing 0 and 1, (b) rectifiable arcs I from 0 to 1 in D̄ meeting ∂D only at 1, and (c) the normalised maps f.

In modern terms this is the conformal welding problem for a disc welded to itself along two adjacent boundary arcs (the 'zipper' or slit-welding problem). It is meant as an elementary building block for 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes': constructing or deforming Riemann surfaces by cutting along arcs and regluing.
errors: The converse in B) and the Scholie bijection (a)<->(b) cannot hold as stated. Any monotone homeomorphism of an interval has bounded variation, so 'rectifiable' is not a genuine restriction on φ. Yet not every homeomorphism is a conformal welding: non-weldable homeomorphisms are known, and existence is guaranteed only under conditions such as quasisymmetry (Pfluger; Lehto–Virtanen).

The map arc → φ is injective for rectifiable slits, since rectifiable arcs are conformally removable. Its image, however, has no known simple characterisation, and rectifiability of I does not correspond to any simple property of φ. So the claimed 1-1 correspondence is at best injective, with the image left uncharacterised.
Minor: the source of f_φ is written D but must be the closed disc D̄, since f is evaluated at ζ, ζ̄ ∈ ∂D.

ideas.what: Boundary correspondence of the Riemann map of a slit Jordan domain: the two banks of the slit correspond to two arcs of the circle, normalised by the symmetric triple 1, ζ, ζ̄
ideas.modern_name: Carathéodory prime-end extension for slit domains

ideas.what: Uniqueness via simple transitivity of Aut(D) on cyclically ordered triples of points of S¹
ideas.modern_name: Simple transitivity of PSU(1,1) on oriented boundary triples

ideas.what: The homeomorphism φ: β → β̄ identifying the two preimages of each slit point; the converse problem of realising a given φ by a slit
ideas.modern_name: Conformal welding (self-welding / zipper welding along a slit)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960), Lehto–Virtanen (1960); later the Marshall–Rohde zipper and Sheffield's quantum zipper

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck independently arrives at the conformal welding problem for a slit, as a tool for conformal surgery. This is classical (1960s) welding theory, and his existence claim is incorrect as stated. It is of historical interest only, showing his analytic approach to building Riemann surfaces in 1983–84.
transcription_corrections: 'f = f_φ : D → D' should be read with closed discs D̄ → D̄ (bar likely omitted in the hand).
In NB2 the word before 'canonique' is crossed out; the surviving reading is 'un [isomorphisme/homéo] canonique φ : β = (1,ζ) ≃ β̄ = (1,ζ̄)'.
Last line likely reads '1) f|D° soit une injection holomorphe' ('holo' struck).
